messages:
Maria: FYI starting RC deploy to staging (rc/2026-03-20). Deploybot just paused the canary due to a flagged transitive package in the SBOM.

deploy-bot: HOLD triggered by policy 'supplychain:vuln-threshold' - component: trans-lib@1.2.3, issue: CVE-2026-9999 (severity: high, vector: network). Canary blocked.

Chris: Can we confirm exploitability from our runtime surface? trans-lib is only a dev/test helper (build-time only) AFAIK. If it never ships in runtime artifact maybe low risk.

Sam: Agree we need artifact inspection. Jenna can you run the sbom diff and the container image content check? Quick commands:

```
# generate SBOM diff against baseline
slsa sbom diff --baseline sbom/stable.json --candidate sbom/rc-2026-03-20.json
# list packages in final image
docker run --rm rc-2026-03-20 sh -c 'ls /app /usr/local/lib || true'
```

Jenna: Running now, should have results in ~3m. If trans-lib is absent from the runtime image this is likely a build-only transitive and lower priority.

deploy-bot: Additional metadata: source repo=infra/tools, build_id=ci-4821, provenance=unverified-transitive-digest. Policy requires either (1) patch/pin the transitive to a fixed digest with SBOM update, (2) produce a QA/SEC exception approved by legal, or (3) rollback to previous build.

Leo: For release planning - we only have the 2-hour change window. If option (1) is quick (<30m) we should pin and continue. If not, we might delay the canary and push a hotfix in the next change window.

Chris: Quick triage from Sec: CVE-2026-9999 has a public PoC but affects only runtime path when trans-lib is present in container. If Jenna's image scan shows it's not present -> low urgency. If it is present and reachable we should not canary.

Jenna: Image scan output: trans-lib NOT found in /app or /usr/local/lib. SBOM shows it under build-deps only. Evidence attached (snippet):

```
# sbom excerpt
- name: trans-lib
  version: 1.2.3
  relationship: build-dependency
```

Maria: Good — that lowers the priority. But deploy-bot still requires either a pin or an exception because provenance is unverified. Two concrete paths: 
A) Update lockfile to pin trans-lib to patched 1.2.4 (or digest), rebuild CI, regenerate SBOM (expected ~20-30m), then resume canary.
B) Request a one-off SEC+Legal exception for this RC (requires manual approval and a mitigation plan), then we can proceed without rebuild.

Chris: From Sec side, I'd prefer path A — consistent and removes the policy trigger. We'll sign off on quick pin.

legal-bot: Automated check: legal approval required for exceptions involving supply chain risk. To request an exception, submit legal-exception form and include mitigation steps and timeframe. Expected turnaround 1-6 hours.

Sam: Operational note: If we choose A make sure the dedupe cache key or build cache isn't reusing the old transitive digest; we need a clean build to certify SBOM. Use `CI_FORCE_CLEAN=true` in the rebuild.

Maria: OK I'll trigger a quick lockfile update and rebuild. Plan: bump trans-lib to 1.2.4 in infra/tools/package-lock.json, run CI (clean), regenerate SBOM, push artifact, then redeploy canary. Will update release notes with: "Fixed transitive build dep security issue (trans-lib 1.2.4) — no user-facing changes."

Leo: :thumbsup: sounds good. If rebuild fails, fallback is to pause RC and schedule hotfix for next change window.

Maria: Starting patch now. ETA ~25m. tagging @Chris @Sam @Jenna for quick verification after CI completes.

(25m later)

Jenna: CI finished, SBOM regenerated. New SBOM shows trans-lib@1.2.4 pinned and provenance verified. Image scan confirms no runtime inclusion.

deploy-bot: HOLD cleared - policy 'supplychain:vuln-threshold' satisfied. Canary resumed to 10% traffic. build_id=ci-4821.2

Maria: Canary passing basic health checks. Rolling notes: "rc/2026-03-20 — security: pinned trans-lib to 1.2.4 to mitigate CVE-2026-9999; no runtime impact observed." Will monitor for 1h then promote.

Chris: Thanks team. Filing a short blameless blurb for the runbook: prefer pin+clean-rebuild for build-only transitive flags to avoid exception delays.

Sam: I'll add a CI guard to set CI_FORCE_CLEAN when supply-chain policy triggers to avoid stale caches.

Maria: Closing thread once promote completes. Thanks everyone.
